source_span: Cuzick’s test for trend ( Cuzick , 1985 ) is a non-parametric test for significant ordering of groups in an increasing or decreasing manner ( two-tailed ) , and was used to assess significance of ordering of behavioral metrics according to the four beta target .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes a key statistical method used to link beta power groupings to behavioral outcomes, central to the study's analysis.

fact: Trials were grouped into quartiles based on beta power estimates to test whether movement onset times varied systematically with beta power levels.
source_span: trials are assigned group labels according to which quartile their power estimate for a particular frequency band falls in . For Figure 5a–c , non-normalized beta is computed in a window including the last 800 ms of the neurofeedback epoch . Trials were assigned labels depending on where they fell in the distribution of non-normalized beta power across trials: 0-25th percentile: label: 1 , 25th – 50th percentile: label: 2 , 50th – 75th percentile: label: 3 , and 75th – 100th percentile: label: 4 .
selection_reasoning: This fact summarizes a key experimental grouping strategy used to analyze the relationship between beta power and movement timing.

fact: Spiking activity was compared between neurofeedback-induced beta oscillations and naturally occurring beta oscillations during reaching tasks to assess differences in firing rates.
source_span: To assess whether units exhibited the same mean firing rate during neurofeedback-induced or naturally occurring beta oscillations , spiking activity was binned into 100 ms bins during NR trials and CO reaching trials . Spike counts during the slow , on-beta bins in the neurofeedback epoch of the NR task were compared with spike counts during slow , on-beta time points during the CO task .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes a principal comparison central to understanding how beta oscillations affect neural firing in different contexts.

fact: A beta amplitude-to-spike rate mapping was estimated for individual units in both neurofeedback and reaching tasks to characterize how beta oscillations influence neural firing rates.
source_span: To assess how individual units were influenced by ongoing beta oscillations in different task contexts , a beta amplitude-to-spike rate mapping was estimated for each unit in the two different tasks .

fact: Beta amplitude was estimated using a bandpass filter from 25 to 40 Hz and the Hilbert transform applied to neural signals during task trials.
source_span: Continuous beta amplitude was estimated for these time slices using a fifth order Butterworth bandpass filter from 25 to 40 Hz and then applying the Hilbert transform .

fact: The stability of the beta amplitude-to-spike rate relationship was assessed by comparing linear regression slopes derived from two non-overlapping data segments within the same task.

The slopes from the resultant linear regressions were plotted against one another .

fact: A logistic regression classifier was trained on spiking activity to distinguish pre-movement onset from post-movement onset periods during different motor tasks in monkeys.
source_span: To assess the information about movement onset contained in spiking activity during different parts of the NR and CO tasks , a logistic regression classifier was trained on spiking activity to discriminate pre-movement onset ( PreMO ) and post-movement onset ( PostMO ) .

fact: Spiking activity was recorded and processed from monkeys performing center-out (CO) and no-reward (NR) reaching tasks to study neural correlates of movement onset.

source_span: For Monkey C , there was very limited CO task data , so fitting the beta amplitude-to-spike rate mapping with a subset yielded unstable inter-task correlations . Using 75% of data in each subset yielded more stable correlations and was used in Figure 6f–h and subsequent statistics .

However , we can learn that we have to point a certain extent to the right for blue targets and to the left for red ones in order to “hit” them [9] . In other words we can learn the association between the target colours , i . e . the contextual cues , and the leftward and rightward mappings . When , after training , either of these target colours is presented , we immediately switch to the correct mapping without the need for feedback to correct our movements .
selection_reasoning: This fact illustrates the general ability to learn cue-mapping associations, relevant to the study's context.

fact: Most previous studies on visuomotor learning used discrete contextual cues with only two states, limiting tests of generalisation to novel conditions.
source_span: It is important to note , however , that in most of these studies the role of the learned associations was investigated for only two discrete association-stimulus/visuomotor-mapping pairings . That is , in many of these studies , the context cue could often only have one of two discrete states: the presence or absence of the cue . In this case , testing conditions cannot go beyond the specifically trained pairings to see how the trained pairings generalise to novel conditions ( a cue cannot be half present ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact motivates the current study's use of continuous cues to explore generalisation.

fact: Continuous contextual cues, like target shape, allow investigation of how learning generalises beyond trained pairings and how the number of pairings affects learning rate.
source_span: However , many cues , like the location of targets when learning the distortions for a single pair of glasses , can vary in a continuous manner . The question arises how learning for a discrete number of trained pairings affects the learning rate and generalises to novel conditions on the same continuous cue scale .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the rationale for studying continuous cues and learning dynamics.

fact: Applying a simple linear rule to generalise visuomotor mappings may not always be beneficial due to complex nonlinearities in the relationship between sensory input and motor output.
source_span: For instance , around the edges of the magnifying glasses large non-linearities in the structure arise . In this respect , applying a general linear rule would not always be beneficial and it might even be better not to generalise beyond the trained conditions at all .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the complexity of generalisation and the potential limits of simple linear models.

fact: Generalisation in visuomotor tasks can vary depending on the cues used, with limited generalisation often found when cues are task-relevant or discrete.
source_span: Very limited generalisation was also found for different starting positions of the movements [22] , different movement speeds [23] , trained left or right hand [13 , 23] and type of movement , i . e . overhand or underhand throwing [13] . The problem with many of these studies , however , is that the cues for the separate mappings were directly task relevant ( e . g . target location and movement speed directly relate to the movement requirements ) , and in some cases even discrete ( e . g . hand used , type of throw ) .
selection_reasoning: This background explains why the study chose a different approach to investigate generalisation, addressing limitations in previous research.

fact: Pre-existing associations from everyday experience with task-relevant cues can interfere with experimental learning and generalisation in visuomotor tasks.
source_span: Using task relevant cues poses a problem in the sense that learned associations between the used cues and visuomotor behaviour will likely pre-exist before training starts , simply through experience in normal life . For instance , to interact with objects we often use our left and right hand independently , and from this experience a separate mapping for each hand could already exist with which generalisation of learning for one hand only would have to compete .
selection_reasoning: This motivates the study's use of task-irrelevant cues to avoid confounding effects of pre-existing associations.

selection_reasoning: This fact explains a key experimental design element aimed at promoting automatic motor learning, relevant to understanding the study's approach.

fact: Participants were trained to associate different visual shapes with specific spatial mappings that shifted visual feedback of their pointing movements.
source_span: For Experiment 1, these learning trials could embrace one of two possible training shape-mapping combinations: one training combination was a shape with ρ = 0.125 ... and a mapping of −75 mm ... the other training combination was shape ρ = 0.875 ... and a mapping of +75 mm.
selection_reasoning: This fact describes the core experimental manipulation central to the study's investigation of shape-mapping learning.

fact: The study tested whether participants could transfer learned shape-mapping associations to new, untrained shapes without visual feedback.
source_span: The other 60 trials were catch trials in which we tested the transfer of training to other target shapes. On catch trials participants did not receive any visual feedback indicating the pointing end-point ...
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights a principal research question about generalization of learned sensorimotor mappings.

fact: Participants were motivated to improve performance by displaying cumulative scores and a high-score list during breaks between blocks.
source_span: During these breaks participants had access to their scores from previous blocks as well as to a hi-score list in which the 10 best scores over all participants were listed anonymously.
selection_reasoning: This fact explains how motivation was maintained, which is important for interpreting learning outcomes.

fact: In Experiment 1, twelve participants with normal or corrected vision and no visuomotor deficits completed the task without being informed about the meaning of different shapes.
source_span: In Experiment 1 twelve observers participated who had normal or corrected-to-normal vision and no known history of visuomotor deficits. The participants were not informed about the different shapes nor about the shape’s meaning in terms of required pointing behaviour.
selection_reasoning: This fact provides essential participant and procedural background relevant to the study's validity and interpretation.

fact: In Experiment 2, two groups of participants were trained with either two or five shape-mapping pairs spanning the same training range.
source_span: In Experiment 2, we tested two different training conditions, each for a new group of 8 participants ... In the 2-Pair Condition, two training shape-mapping contingencies were used ... In the 5-Pair Condition, five shape-mapping pairs spanned the same training range as the 2-Pair Condition ...
selection_reasoning: This fact describes a key experimental manipulation testing the effect of training complexity on learning.

fact: In Experiment 3, participants were trained on three shape-mapping pairs with intermediate mapping values.
source_span: In Experiment 3, six participants were trained on three shape-mapping pairs: (ρ = 0.375, mapping = −37.5mm), (ρ = 0.625, mapping = 37.5mm) and (ρ = 0.875, mapping = 112.5mm).
selection_reasoning: This fact outlines another experimental condition relevant to understanding the study's exploration of shape-mapping learning.

fact: Participants in Experiments 2 and 3 were informed that different shapes required different pointing behaviors but had to deduce the specific shape-mapping contingencies themselves.
source_span: In Experiment 2 and 3 participants were informed about the fact that different shapes would need different pointing behaviours. However, participants were not informed about the particular shape-mapping contingencies, which they had to deduce themselves.
selection_reasoning: This fact clarifies participant knowledge and learning conditions, important for interpreting learning mechanisms.

fact: The study modeled learning of shape-mapping contingencies using a Mixture-of-Kalman-Filters approach, where each shape is associated with its own Kalman Filter.
source_span: Here we modelled the learning of the shape-mapping contingencies as a Mixture-of-Kalman-Filters in which each shape is coupled to its own Kalman Filter.
selection_reasoning: This fact describes the key computational modeling approach used to understand the learning process.

fact: The Kalman Filter model integrates sensory feedback and prior experience weighted by their respective precisions to optimally update estimates of required mappings.
source_span: The Kalman Filter ... takes into account the precision of the current internal estimate of the required mapping ... as well as the precision of the incoming information in the form of sensory feedback, which is used to update that estimate.
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the theoretical basis for the computational model central to the study's interpretation.

fact: The study modeled learning of shape-mapping contingencies using a Mixture-of-Kalman-Filters, where each shape is associated with its own Kalman Filter.
source_span: Here we modelled the learning of the shape-mapping contingencies as a Mixture-of-Kalman-Filters in which each shape is coupled to its own Kalman Filter.
selection_reasoning: This describes the core modeling approach used to understand how shape-mapping learning occurs, which is central to the study.

fact: The Kalman Filter updates internal estimates by combining prior knowledge and sensory feedback, accounting for their respective uncertainties.
source_span: The Kalman Filter [45] is such an adaptive procedure that takes into account the precision of the current internal estimate of the required mapping ( the “prior” as it were , at that specific point in time ) as well as the precision of the incoming information in the form of sensory feedback , which is used to update that estimate.
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the key mechanism behind the learning model, important for understanding the study's rationale.

fact: The model assumes that perception of shape is noisy, causing learning for one shape to influence neighboring shapes in a graded manner.
source_span: To describe the behaviour of the Mixture-of-Kalman-Filters across the target shapes , it is important to note that the perception of the shape is noisy and thus cannot singularly influence one filter only . That is , learning for one shape will also affect the filters of neighbouring shapes in a graded fashion.
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights a key assumption and mechanism explaining generalization across shapes, which is central to the study's findings.

fact: The model incorporates shape discrimination thresholds to link generalization across shapes to perceptual noise in shape perception.
source_span: Note that we chose a similar dependence on shape-difference for the generalisation function , which is normally used in Gaussian distributions ... in order to directly link the generalisation across shapes to the shape discrimination threshold σρ ( see Supporting S2 Text ).
selection_reasoning: This fact connects perceptual limitations to the model's generalization predictions, important for interpreting results.

fact: The model predicts generalization patterns and learning rates based on the number of training pairs and individual participant parameters.
source_span: We used the model to make predictions for the generalisation patterns as well as the learning rates and how they depend on the number of training pairs.
selection_reasoning: This fact summarizes the main application of the model to generate testable predictions, a principal finding.

fact: The learning rate in the model is determined by the ratio between visual/motor noise and process noise parameters.
source_span: In this case the model had one free parameter per participant , i . e . the ratio between σy0 and σ p r o c e s s 2 which determines the learning rate.
selection_reasoning: This fact identifies a key parameter controlling learning speed, relevant for understanding individual differences and model fitting.

fact: Shape likelihood is modeled as a Gaussian distribution reflecting uncertainty in shape perception, influencing the weighted response from each Kalman Filter.
source_span: Shape likelihood: P ( ρ | ρ t ) = N ( ρ | ρ t , σ ρ ) ... Model response: MR ( ρ t ) = ∑ KF ( ρ ) E ( KF ( ρ ) ) P ( ρ | ρ t )
selection_reasoning: This fact explains how the model accounts for perceptual uncertainty in selecting responses, a key mechanism in the study.

fact: The study tested a Mixture-of-Kalman-Filters model to simulate individual participants' learning responses using trial sequences from a shape discrimination experiment.
source_span: For the Mixture-of-Kalman-Filters Model , we simulated the sequence of responses using the trial sequences ( i . e . the order of training shapes ) exactly as they had been used for the individual participants in the experiment ( including catch trials ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes a key method used to model participant learning, central to the study's approach.

fact: The learning rate in the model was determined by fitting a single free parameter per participant, the ratio between sensory noise and process noise.
source_span: The best fit for each participant was obtained by fitting the ratio between σy0 and σprocess that determines the learning rate ( one free parameter per participant ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains a core model parameter critical to understanding how learning was quantified.

fact: The model included 100 Kalman Filters spanning the entire shape space from very spiky to circular shapes to capture shape discrimination learning.
source_span: For the simulations 100 Kalman Filters were included in the mixture , spanning the available shape-space in its entirety ( from ρ = 0 . 01 , a very spiky shape , to ρ = 1 . 0 for circular shapes ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the model's design to cover the full stimulus range, important for interpreting the learning mechanism.

fact: The study tested the hypothesis that learning and transfer of learning occur in a linear fashion by performing ANOVAs on residuals from linear regression fits to participant data.
source_span: To test the hypothesis for linear generalisation directly , ANOVA’s were performed on the residuals of all trials in the last trial-block , i . e . including catch trials . If the learning and transfer of learning occurs in a linear fashion there should not be any difference in the residuals between the different shapes used in the experiment .
selection_reasoning: This fact states the main research question about the nature of learning generalization.

fact: If the ANOVA on residuals shows significant differences between shapes, the hypothesis of linear generalisation can be rejected.
source_span: Thus , if the ANOVA leads to a significant result the hypothesis for linear generalisation can be rejected .
selection_reasoning: This fact clarifies the criterion for accepting or rejecting the linear generalisation hypothesis, central to interpreting results.

fact: The model's predictions about how the number of training pairs influences learning rates were made using a fixed ratio between sensory noise and process noise.
source_span: Predictions for the influence of the number of training pairs on the learning rates were made using a fixed ratio between σy0 and σprocess 2 for the model simulations .
selection_reasoning: This fact relates to the study's approach to predicting learning dynamics, important for understanding the model's application.

fact: Neglected tropical diseases (NTDs) affect an estimated 2.7 billion of the world's poorest people, causing significant physical debilitation, lowered economic productivity, and social ostracism.
source_span: Neglected tropical diseases ( NTDs ) are parasitic and bacterial diseases that affect an estimated 2 . 7 billion of the world's poorest people , causing significant physical debilitation , lowered economic productivity , and social ostracism for afflicted individuals [1] .
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the global burden and importance of NTDs, motivating the study.

fact: Five NTDs with available preventive chemotherapy—lymphatic filariasis (LF), trachoma, schistosomiasis, onchocerciasis, and soil-transmitted helminths (STH)—have been targeted for control or elimination.
source_span: Five NTDs with available preventive chemotherapy: lymphatic filariasis ( LF ) , trachoma , schistosomiasis , onchocerciasis and the three soil-transmitted helminths ( STH ) ; have been targeted for control or elimination , but resource constraints in endemic countries have impeded progress toward these goals [2] .
selection_reasoning: This fact defines the diseases targeted by control programs, framing the study's disease focus.

fact: Resource constraints in endemic countries have impeded progress toward control and elimination goals for NTDs.
source_span: Five NTDs with available preventive chemotherapy... have been targeted for control or elimination, but resource constraints in endemic countries have impeded progress toward these goals [2].
selection_reasoning: This highlights the problem motivating the development of more efficient mapping methods.

fact: Mass drug administration (MDA) of at-risk populations with safe and effective drugs is the core public health strategy to fight the five targeted NTDs.
source_span: At the core of public health efforts to fight the five NTDs mentioned above is a strategy of mass drug administration ( MDA ) of at-risk populations with safe and effective drugs often donated by pharmaceutical companies [5] .
selection_reasoning: This explains the main intervention approach relevant to the study.

fact: Before launching MDA, countries must demonstrate that the disease threshold for public health intervention, as established by WHO, has been surpassed.
source_span: Before an MDA can be launched , a country must demonstrate that the disease threshold for public health intervention , as established by the World Health Organization ( WHO ) , has been surpassed [6] , [7] .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains why mapping and threshold determination are critical.

fact: Currently, each NTD program has its own mapping methodology, which can be costly and burdensome when multiple surveys are needed in the same country.
source_span: Currently , each NTD program has its own methodology [8] . Conducting multiple surveys in the same country can be costly and burdensome to national disease programs .
selection_reasoning: This motivates the need for an integrated mapping approach.

fact: Because NTDs tend to overlap geographically, an integrated mapping approach could result in significant resource savings and more efficient identification of populations needing treatment.
source_span: Because NTDs tend to overlap in geographic areas , it is logical that an integrated approach to mapping NTDs might result in more efficient identification of populations needing treatment [9] .
selection_reasoning: This provides the rationale for developing an integrated mapping protocol.

fact: We developed and field-tested an innovative integrated NTD mapping protocol called Integrated Threshold Mapping (ITM) Methodology for lymphatic filariasis, trachoma, schistosomiasis, and soil-transmitted helminths.
source_span: We developed and field-tested an innovative integrated NTD mapping protocol ( Integrated Threshold Mapping ( ITM ) Methodology ) for lymphatic filariasis ( LF ) , trachoma , schistosomiasis and soil-transmitted helminths ( STH ) .
selection_reasoning: This states the main methodological innovation of the study.

fact: The ITM protocol is designed to be resource-efficient and aims to determine whether a disease has reached the threshold to trigger public health interventions in an implementation unit.
source_span: The protocol is designed to be resource-efficient , and its specific purpose is to determine whether a threshold to trigger public health interventions in an implementation unit has been attained .
selection_reasoning: This clarifies the purpose and advantage of the ITM protocol.

fact: The ITM protocol relies on WHO-recommended indicators in disease-specific age groups and uses the district as the sampling frame, except for schistosomiasis where the sub-district is used.
source_span: The protocol relies on World Health Organization ( WHO ) recommended indicators in the disease-specific age groups . For each disease , the sampling frame was the district , but for schistosomiasis , the sub-district rather than the ecological zone was used .
selection_reasoning: This describes the high-level design of the ITM protocol relevant to its validity.

fact: We tested the ITM protocol by comparing it to current WHO mapping methodologies for each targeted disease in one district each in Mali and Senegal.
source_span: We tested the protocol by comparing it to current WHO mapping methodologies for each of the targeted diseases in one district each in Mali and Senegal .
selection_reasoning: This states the key comparative evaluation approach.

fact: The ITM methodology reached the same conclusions as the WHO methodologies regarding the initiation of public health interventions for trachoma, lymphatic filariasis, and soil-transmitted helminths.
source_span: In this study , the ITM methodology reached the same conclusions as the WHO methodologies regarding the initiation of public health interventions for trachoma , LF and STH ...
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding validating the ITM approach.

fact: The ITM methodology resulted in more targeted intervention recommendations for schistosomiasis compared to the WHO methodologies.
source_span: In this study , the ITM methodology ... resulted in more targeted intervention recommendations for schistosomiasis .
selection_reasoning: This highlights a key difference and potential advantage of ITM for schistosomiasis.

fact: The ITM methodology was practical, feasible, and demonstrated overall cost savings compared with the standard, non-integrated WHO methodologies.
source_span: ITM was practical , feasible and demonstrated an overall cost saving compared with the standard , non-integrated , WHO methodologies .
selection_reasoning: This supports the significance and potential impact of ITM.

fact: This integrated mapping tool could facilitate the implementation of much-needed NTD programs in endemic countries.
source_span: This integrated mapping tool could facilitate the implementation of much-needed programs in endemic countries .
selection_reasoning: This states the broader significance and potential public health impact.

fact: Trachoma was assessed by examining children aged 1–9 years for active trachoma and females aged 15 years or older for trichiasis using the WHO Simplified Grading System.
source_span: For trachoma , an ophthalmic technician examined both eyes of children aged 1–9 years for clinical signs of active trachoma ( trachomatous inflammation follicular [TF] ) and of females aged ≥15 years for clinical signs of trichiasis ( trachomatous trichiasis [TT] ) using a binocular loupe and natural light according to the WHO Simplified Grading System [12] .
selection_reasoning: This describes the disease context and key diagnostic method for trachoma, a core background and method relevant to the study.

fact: Schistosoma haematobium infection in children aged 6–9 years was detected by testing for haematuria in urine samples using reagent strips.
source_span: For Schistosoma haematobium , the presence of haematuria in urine samples from children aged 6–9 years was detected by urine reagent strips .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides background on the diagnostic approach for a key parasitic infection studied, relevant to understanding the methods.

fact: The prevalence and egg load of Schistosoma mansoni and soil-transmitted helminths (STH) were measured using the Kato-Katz method.
source_span: For Schistosoma mansoni and STH , the prevalence and egg load ( eggs per gram of feces ) were calculated using the Kato-Katz method [14] .
selection_reasoning: This describes a key diagnostic method for important parasitic infections, relevant to the study's approach.

fact: Children found to have active trachoma were treated with tetracycline ointment applied twice daily for six weeks.
source_span: Children who were found to have active trachoma received two tubes of tetracycline ointment , to be applied twice daily for a period of six weeks .
selection_reasoning: This fact relates to the clinical management and significance of detecting active trachoma in the study.

fact: Females diagnosed with trichiasis were referred to health centers for trichiasis surgery.
source_span: Females found to have trichiasis were referred to the nearest health center that provides trichiasis surgery .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the clinical relevance and follow-up care linked to the study findings.

fact: Persons testing positive for Wuchereria bancrofti antigen and children infected with Schistosoma haematobium, Schistosoma mansoni, or soil-transmitted helminths were referred to district health centers if mass drug administration (MDA) was not planned.
source_span: Persons who tested positive for W . bancrofti antigen and children who were found to be infected with S . haematobium , S . mansoni or STH were referred to the district health center in case an MDA was not planned in the district .
selection_reasoning: This fact connects diagnostic results to public health interventions, showing translational significance.

fact: The study compared two methodologies, the ITM and WHO methods, for mapping neglected tropical diseases including trachoma, schistosomiasis, soil-transmitted helminths, and lymphatic filariasis.
source_span: Results for trachoma , STH and LF were analyzed at the district level for both methodologies ... The public health interventions based on the WHO thresholds ... were compared for both methodologies .
selection_reasoning: This fact summarizes the main study question and approach comparing two mapping methodologies.

fact: In Banamba District, Mali, both ITM and WHO methodologies indicated no need for mass drug administration (MDA) for trachoma or soil-transmitted helminths, but both indicated a need for trichiasis surgeries.
source_span: As shown in Figure 3 , the results of both methodologies indicated no need for MDA for trachoma ( ITM Method: 1 . 9% , WHO method: 4 . 7% ... or STH: 0% , 0% ) within the surveyed district . The methodologies were also concordant in indicating a need for TT surgeries ( ITM Method: 2 . 6% , WHO Method: 3 . 7% ... ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact reports principal findings comparing the two methods for key diseases in a study site.

fact: The ITM and WHO methodologies differed in their indication of the need for schistosomiasis treatment in Banamba District, with the ITM method identifying more sub-districts requiring mass drug administration for the whole population.
source_span: Because the ITM method had as its purpose to refine the schistosomiasis mapping , the two methods differed , in indicating a need for schistosomiasis treatment: the WHO methodology indicated a need for MDA for schistosomiasis among only school-aged children in the entire area . The ITM methodology indicated that four sub-districts were in need of MDA for schistosomiasis among school-aged children only , and that five sub-districts were in need of MDA for schistosomiasis for the whole population .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights a key difference in mapping outcomes with implications for treatment scope.

fact: Treating the whole population in sub-districts identified by the ITM methodology for schistosomiasis would result in nearly 33,500 additional at-risk persons being treated compared to treating only school-aged children as indicated by the WHO methodology.
source_span: Treating the whole population in the sub-districts where this was indicated by the integrated mapping protocol would result in nearly 33 , 500 additional at-risk persons being treated than if only school-aged children in these sub-districts were treated ( as indicated by the WHO protocol ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact quantifies the public health impact of the differing mapping methodologies.

fact: In Diourbel District, Senegal, both ITM and WHO methodologies indicated the need for mass drug administration for trachoma and the need for trichiasis surgeries, but no need for intervention for soil-transmitted helminths.
source_span: Both methodologies indicated the need for MDA for trachoma in the surveyed district ( ITM Method: 14 . 9% , WHO Method: 13 . 4% ... ) and both methodologies indicated that there was no need for intervention for STH: 0% , 0% . Both ITM and WHO methodologies were also concordant regarding the need for TT surgeries ( ITM Method: 4 . 7% , WHO Method: 6 . 1% ... ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact reports key comparative findings in a second study site, supporting the study's principal results.

fact: The lymphatic filariasis (LF) mapping was included to validate the feasibility of the integrated mapping approach but not to validate the disease prevalence results.
source_span: The LF mapping was added to validate the feasibility of the integrated mapping and not to validate the results .
selection_reasoning: This clarifies the purpose of including LF mapping, relevant to understanding study design and interpretation.

fact: The Integrated Threshold Mapping (ITM) methodology is an operational tool designed for Ministries of Health in NTD-endemic countries to determine if the threshold for launching disease-specific public health interventions has been reached.
source_span: We describe an integrated NTD mapping methodology ( Integrated Threshold Mapping ) that can be used as an operational tool by Ministries of Health in NTD-endemic countries to determine if the threshold needed to launch disease-specific public health intervenions has been reached .
selection_reasoning: This fact defines the main purpose and significance of the ITM methodology, which is central to the study.

fact: The ITM methodology balances epidemiologic rigor with field practicality to provide a simpler and quicker way for Ministries of Health to estimate their neglected tropical disease (NTD) needs.
source_span: In developing this ITM methodology , we sought to balance epidemiologic rigour with field practicality , resulting in an approach that can be used only for determining where public health interventions are needed .
selection_reasoning: This explains the motivation and design principle behind the ITM method, important for understanding why it was developed.

fact: The ITM methodology retains key indicators and age groups from WHO disease-specific mapping guidelines but adapts the sampling methodologies to improve practicality.
source_span: With the exception of some minor modifications for trachoma , we have retained the key indicators and age groups used in the disease-specific WHO mapping guidelines , but have adapted the sampling methodologies .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the methodological approach and how ITM relates to existing WHO protocols.

fact: The ITM methodology reduces costs, manpower, and resource needs compared to the WHO methodology, providing cost savings of 31% in Mali and 19% in Senegal.
source_span: The results of the cost data analysis Table 4 , indicate that using the ITM methodology resulted in a 31% overall cost savings in Mali ( $6 , 968 vs . $10 , 039 ) , and a 19% overall cost savings in Senegal ( $8 , 442 vs . $10 , 372 ) .
selection_reasoning: Cost reduction is a key practical advantage and a principal finding relevant to public health implementation.

fact: The ITM methodology used resources more efficiently than the WHO methodology in travel, supplies, and team training in both Mali and Senegal.
source_span: In both countries , the ITM methodology used resources more efficiently than the WHO methodology in the areas of travel , supplies and team training , as shown in Table 4 .
selection_reasoning: This supports the significance of ITM's efficiency improvements, important for policy and implementation.

fact: In Mali, the ITM methodology identified more sub-districts needing mass drug administration (MDA) for schistosomiasis, including some for whole population treatment, compared to the WHO methodology which recommended MDA only for school-aged children.
source_span: The WHO methodology indicated a need for MDA for schistosomiasis treatment among only school-aged children in the entire area , while the ITM methodology indicated six sub-districts in need of MDA for schistosomiasis among school-aged children only , four sub-districts in need of MDA for schistosomiasis for the whole population and one sub-district which did not pass the threshold for treatment .
selection_reasoning: This finding shows a key difference in public health recommendations between ITM and WHO methods, relevant to intervention targeting.

fact: Compared to the district-based WHO protocol, the ITM methodology targeted nearly 46,000 extra at-risk individuals for schistosomiasis treatment in Mali.
source_span: Compared to the district based WHO protocol , the ITM methodology targeted nearly 46 , 000 extra at-risk individuals for treatment .
selection_reasoning: This quantifies the increased reach of ITM, a principal finding with public health significance.

fact: The ITM methodology uses program-specific age groups as indicated by WHO, with minor adaptations for trachoma, to allow use of WHO thresholds and reduce the number of people undergoing multiple tests.
source_span: In our ITM mapping protocol , we insisted on using the program-specific age groups as indicated by WHO with the exception of some adaptation for trachoma . The advantage of using these established age groups was that the WHO thresholds were applicable and that few people had to undergo multiple tests and examinations; only in a limited number of cases were people asked to undergo more than one test or examination .
selection_reasoning: This clarifies a key methodological choice that supports the validity and practicality of ITM.

fact: The ITM protocol uses a convenience sample in each village to facilitate data collection and improve time efficiency compared to house-to-house visits used in the WHO trachoma protocol.
source_span: In each village , we chose to use a convenience sample for reasons of field practicality . Asking people of different ages to come to a central location in each village facilitated data collection and was much more time-efficient than house-to-house visits , such as those used in the WHO trachoma protocol .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains a key adaptation in sampling that improves field practicality, relevant to the study's main question.

fact: The ITM and WHO methodologies resulted in the same public health recommendations in the field testing conducted in Mali and Senegal.
source_span: As the field testing in both countries showed , the data of both methodologies resulted in the same public health recommendations .
selection_reasoning: This principal finding supports the validity of ITM as an alternative to WHO protocols.

fact: The ITM protocol is not designed to provide epidemiologically correct prevalence data or to serve as a baseline for measuring impact at the district level.
source_span: To understand the value and limitations of this protocol , it is critical to understand that this protocol is not claiming to provide epidemiologically correct prevalence data because both the villages and the individuals tested were not randomly selected . First , this implies that we cannot recommend using findings from this methodology as a baseline for measuring impact at the district level .
selection_reasoning: This limitation is important for interpreting the scope and appropriate use of ITM results.

fact: The ITM protocol maintains the WHO-recommended disease indicators and thresholds for lymphatic filariasis, schistosomiasis, and soil-transmitted helminths but uses a novel sampling frame for more practical field implementation.
source_span: The ITM protocol maintains the WHO-recommended disease indicators and thresholds for LF , schistosomiasis and STH , but we used a novel sampling frame for more practical field implementation .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the methodological innovation and alignment with WHO standards, which is central to the study's approach.

fact: To improve representativeness for the trachomatous inflammation—follicular (TF) indicator, the study selected a predetermined number of children aged 1–5 and 6–9 to prevent biased prevalence estimates.
source_span: To improve the representativeness for the TF indicator , we selected a pre-determined number of children between the ages of 1–5 and 6–9 . This was intended to prevent biased estimates in case the 6–9 year age group made up the majority of children being graded for trachoma because prevalence rates are highest in 1–5 year olds .
selection_reasoning: This fact clarifies a key sampling strategy to ensure accurate disease prevalence measurement, relevant to the study's validity.

fact: The study used women above the age of 15 years to measure trachomatous trichiasis prevalence, based on expert consultation and literature.
source_span: After consultation with trachoma experts , we decided to use women above the age of 15 yrs [22] .
selection_reasoning: This fact defines a key disease indicator measurement choice, important for understanding the study's approach.

fact: The ITM methodology links the sampling frame directly to the implementation unit for mass drug administration (MDA) for each neglected tropical disease to improve public health action feasibility.
source_span: Because the ITM methodology is focused on public health action , the sampling frame is directly linked to the implementation unit for MDA for each of the NTDs .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the practical public health focus of the methodology, central to the study's significance.

fact: The study used the district as the primary implementation unit for soil-transmitted helminths, consistent with WHO recommendations for lymphatic filariasis and trachoma.
source_span: we decided to use the district as the primary implementation unit for STH as it is recommended by WHO for LF and trachoma .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains a key design decision aligning with WHO guidance, relevant to the study's methodology.

fact: Both the ITM and WHO methodologies concluded that no intervention was necessary for soil-transmitted helminths in the two countries studied, confirming the reliability of the ITM methodology.
source_span: Our methodology found the same public health intervention for trachoma and for STH . For STH , both methodologies concluded that no intervention was necessary , which confirmed the reliability of our methodology in the two countries .
selection_reasoning: This fact reports a principal finding validating the new methodology against the WHO standard.

fact: For schistosomiasis, the study recommends using sub-district implementation units for MDA to better target treatment and avoid overtreating or undertreating subpopulations.
source_span: In the case of schistosomiasis , a disease that is very focal in nature , and for which treatment medication is costly and in limited supply , we feel that it would be more appropriate to use the sub-district as implementation units to determine needs for treatment because a district-based approach may result in overtreating or undertreating subpopulations within the district [23] .
selection_reasoning: This fact addresses a key disease-specific recommendation with public health and resource implications.

fact: Using the sub-district as the implementation unit allowed the integrated methodology to identify highly endemic and low endemic sub-areas within districts that the WHO ecological zone approach missed.
source_span: Our results show that by using the sub-district as I . U . , the MDA will be more targeted to people at risk . In our study , when the WHO-recommended ecological zone was used as the implementation unit , highly endemic ( prevalence of >50% ) or low endemic ( prevalence of <10% ) sub-areas of the district were not identified , but were identified by the integrated methodology .
selection_reasoning: This fact demonstrates a key advantage of the integrated methodology in targeting treatment more precisely.

fact: Using the WHO protocol would have resulted in tens of thousands of people in highly endemic areas not receiving treatment and others not in need being treated, as observed in Senegal.
source_span: As a result , using the WHO protocol would have meant that tens of thousands of people living in highly endemic areas would not have received treatment , and that other people not in need of treatment would have been treated , as would have been the case in Senegal .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the public health significance of the integrated approach over the WHO protocol.

fact: The integrated approach was more efficient in cost, transport, time in the field, and use of human resources compared to the WHO methodologies.
source_span: The integrated approach proved to be more efficient in cost , transport , time in the field and the use of human resources .
selection_reasoning: This fact summarizes a principal finding about the operational advantages of the integrated methodology.

fact: The integrated mapping team consisted of five experienced technicians performing multiple tasks, which increased efficiency and reduced the number of vehicles and personnel compared to WHO methodologies.

The Z-scales are a previously published set of descriptors that characterize the physicochemical properties of the amino acids side chains. The resulting scales correlate to lipophilicity, size and polarity for each amino acid.
selection_reasoning: Describes a key methodological step enabling improved sequence representation in the models.

source_span: To determine the effect of individual residues , for each sequence each residue was mutated back to wild type in silico by replacing the descriptors of the mutant amino acid with the descriptors of the corresponding wild type residue ... selection_reasoning: This method provides mechanistic insight into how mutations affect drug resistance, a key scientific contribution.

fact: The study identified novel mutations that lead to an increase in drug resistance fold change on average, after excluding previously known mutations.

selection_reasoning: This fact illustrates variability between assays for clinically relevant drugs, impacting resistance interpretation.

selection_reasoning: This fact relates to the clinical relevance and evaluation of the resistance prediction models.

fact: Staphylococcus aureus expresses multiple cell wall-anchored proteins that mediate adhesion, invasion, and immune evasion, contributing to its virulence.

fact: This study reveals a novel role for ClfB during Staphylococcus aureus skin and soft tissue infections.

selection_reasoning: This is a principal mechanistic finding central to the study's conclusions.

source_span: Targeting ClfB using a model vaccine that induced both protective humoral and cellular responses , leads to protection during S . aureus skin infection .

fact: ClfB is identified as an important antigen for future vaccines against skin and soft tissue infections caused by Staphylococcus aureus.
source_span: This study therefore identifies ClfB as an important antigen for future SSTI vaccines .
selection_reasoning: This summarizes the study's implication for vaccine development.

fact: Staphylococcus aureus is the leading cause of skin and soft tissue infections in humans, resulting in millions of outpatient visits and hundreds of thousands of hospital admissions annually in the United States.
source_span: Staphylococcus aureus is the leading cause of skin and soft tissue infections ( SSTIs ) in humans [1 , 2] with S . aureus SSTIs resulting in over 11 million outpatient visits and almost 500 , 000 hospital admissions in the United States annually [3] .
selection_reasoning: This background fact establishes the public health importance of S. aureus SSTIs.

fact: Staphylococcus aureus skin and soft tissue infections often form cutaneous abscesses that limit antibiotic penetration and efficacy.
source_span: S . aureus SSTIs routinely manifest as cutaneous abscesses which limit the penetration and efficacy of antibiotics [4] .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains why SSTIs are difficult to treat and why alternative therapies like vaccines are needed.

fact: Community-acquired methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (CA-MRSA) skin infections are increasing in healthy individuals and are becoming harder to treat due to antibiotic resistance.
source_span: Community-acquired methicillin resistant S . aureus ( CA-MRSA ) skin infections are increasing in frequency in healthy individuals [5] and the treatment of these infections has become increasingly difficult due to the emergence of antibiotic resistance .
selection_reasoning: This fact motivates the need for vaccine development as an alternative to antibiotics.

fact: An effective universal vaccine against Staphylococcus aureus is unlikely, so vaccines targeting specific clinical manifestations such as skin and soft tissue infections may be more feasible.
source_span: Given the wide spectrum of pathologies caused by this bacterium it is unlikely that a universal anti-S . aureus vaccine will ever be realised [6] , and instead , a vaccine targeting specific clinical manifestations may need to be pursued .
selection_reasoning: This fact frames the rationale for focusing on SSTI-specific vaccine targets like ClfB.

fact: Cell wall-anchored proteins are important for Staphylococcus aureus virulence during skin and soft tissue infections and may be particularly important during abscess formation.
source_span: These studies indicate that CWA proteins are important during SSTIs and suggest that CWA proteins may be particularly important during the process of abscess formation .
selection_reasoning: This supports the study's focus on ClfB, a cell wall-anchored protein.

fact: Clumping factor A (ClfA) plays a role in Staphylococcus aureus skin infection, but vaccines targeting ClfA provide only modest protection, suggesting other surface proteins like ClfB may be important.
source_span: Clumping factor A has previously been shown to play a role in the pathogenesis of S . aureus SSTI , as mice inoculated with a ClfA-deficient mutant of S . aureus strain Newman demonstrated a lower bacterial burden in the skin compared to the wild type strain at Day 2 post-inoculation [11] . selection_reasoning: This fact justifies investigating ClfB as an alternative vaccine target.

fact: ClfB binds to plasma fibrinogen, cytokeratin 10, and loricrin, with loricrin being a critical ligand for ClfB in vivo in mice.
source_span: ClfB binds to plasma fibrinogen [19] , cytokeratin 10 [20] , which is the dominant component of the interior of squamous cells , and to loricrin , which is the most abundant protein of the cornified envelope of squamous cells [21] . Rates of S . aureus nasal colonization were significantly reduced in loricrin-knockout mice compared to wild-type mice , demonstrating that loricrin is a critical ligand for ClfB in vivo , at least in mice [13] .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides mechanistic insight into ClfB's binding partners relevant to infection.

fact: Mice infected with a ClfB-deficient Staphylococcus aureus strain formed significantly smaller abscess lesions and had reduced bacterial burden compared to mice infected with the wild-type strain.
source_span: Mice infected with LAC::lux ΔclfB formed significantly smaller abscess lesions on day 3–6 compared to mice infected with LAC::lux ( Fig 1A and 1B ) . The bioluminescence signal was also reduced in LAC::lux ΔclfB infected animals compared to LAC::lux infected mice ( Fig 1C and 1D ) . The reduction in bioluminescence signal was validated by quantifying the bacterial burden in the skin on day 3 ( Fig 1E ) and day 6 ( Fig 1F ) .
selection_reasoning: This experimental result directly supports the conclusion that ClfB contributes to abscess formation and bacterial load in SSTIs.

fact: ClfB affects both the rate of abscess formation and the overall size of the abscess formed during Staphylococcus aureus skin and soft tissue infections.
source_span: Taken together, these results demonstrate that ClfB affects both the rate of abscess formation and the overall size of the abscess formed, which ultimately leads to greater bacterial burden in the skin.
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding linking ClfB to abscess development and bacterial burden, central to the study's main question and significance.

fact: ClfB has an important function during Staphylococcus aureus skin and soft tissue infections, likely exerting its effect early in the infection process.
source_span: Crucially, these results have demonstrated for the first time that ClfB has an important function during S. aureus SSTIs, likely exerting its effect early in the infection process.
selection_reasoning: This highlights the novel discovery and timing of ClfB's role, important background and main conclusion.

fact: During nasal colonization, Staphylococcus aureus binding to the squamous epithelium is facilitated by the interaction between ClfB and the squamous cell envelope protein loricrin.
source_span: During nasal colonization, S. aureus binding to the squamous epithelium of the anterior nares is facilitated via the interaction between ClfB and the squamous cell envelope protein loricrin.
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the known ClfB-loricrin interaction, providing biological context for the study.

fact: Loricrin is present in the epidermal layer and in the abscess wall structure during Staphylococcus aureus subcutaneous abscess formation.
source_span: At 48 h post-infection loricrin is clearly visible in the epidermal layer of the skin, which is to be expected as it is a major component of the cornified envelope. Interestingly, it is also detected in the abscess wall structure following challenge with both LAC::lux and LAC::lux ΔclfB.
selection_reasoning: This fact supports the relevance of loricrin in the infected tissue, linking to the mechanism of ClfB binding.

fact: Loricrin-deficient mice form significantly smaller abscesses and have reduced bacterial burden during Staphylococcus aureus skin and soft tissue infections compared to wild-type mice.
source_span: Lor-/- mice formed significantly smaller abscesses compared to WT mice and had reduced bioluminescence, indicating the presence of loricrin is important for abscess formation and bacterial burden during S. aureus SSTIs.
selection_reasoning: This finding demonstrates the functional importance of loricrin in infection severity, a key mechanistic and translational claim.

fact: Abscess formation is impaired in loricrin-deficient mice at 12 hours post infection, with less well-structured and smaller abscesses formed.
source_span: Importantly, it can be seen that abscess formation is impaired in Lor-/- mice at 12 hours post infection with overall less well-structured and smaller abscesses being formed.
selection_reasoning: This supports the early role of loricrin in abscess development, reinforcing the mechanism and timing.

fact: In wild-type mice, infection with Staphylococcus aureus lacking ClfB results in smaller abscess lesions and reduced bacterial burden compared to infection with wild-type bacteria.
source_span: WT mice that received LAC::lux ΔclfB formed smaller abscess lesions and had significantly reduced bioluminescence compared to WT mice that received LAC::lux which was confirmed by quantifying bacterial burden in the skin.
selection_reasoning: This shows the direct contribution of ClfB to virulence and abscess severity, a core experimental finding.

fact: In loricrin-deficient mice, there is no significant difference in abscess size or bacterial burden between infection with wild-type Staphylococcus aureus and ClfB-deficient bacteria.
source_span: There was no significant difference in abscess lesion area, bioluminescence or skin CFUs between Lor-/- mice that received LAC::lux or LAC::lux ΔclfB.
selection_reasoning: This indicates that ClfB's effect depends on the presence of loricrin, clarifying the mechanism.

fact: Expression of loricrin within the tissue during abscess formation facilitates the binding of Staphylococcus aureus via ClfB, contributing to the formation of a robust abscess.
source_span: Taken together these data suggest that expression of loricrin within the tissue during abscess formation facilitates the binding of S. aureus specifically via ClfB, thus contributing to the formation of a robust abscess.
selection_reasoning: This summarizes the key mechanistic insight linking host protein and bacterial factor to infection outcome.

fact: Pre-incubation of Staphylococcus aureus with recombinant loricrin loop L2v reduces abscess lesion area and bacterial burden during skin infection in mice.
source_span: Mice that received LAC::lux+L2v had reduced abscess lesion area compared to the LAC::lux+GST group. In addition, bioluminescence signal was reduced throughout the infection period in LAC::lux+L2v infected mice compared to mice that received LAC::lux+GST and this reduction in bioluminescence was confirmed with a significant decrease in the bacterial burden in the skin on day 3 and 6 post-infection.
selection_reasoning: This demonstrates a potential therapeutic approach by blocking ClfB-loricrin interaction, relevant for translational significance.

fact: Vaccination with ClfB combined with the TLR9 agonist CpG induces antigen-specific cellular and humoral immune responses in mice.
source_span: Immunization with ClfB in combination with CpG drove a significant increase in ClfB-specific IFNγ, IL-17 and IL-22 producing CD4+ T cells by inguinal lymph node cells compared to CpG-immunized mice. ClfB-specific CD8+ T cells producing IFNγ, IL-17 and IL-22 were also increased. Vaccination with ClfB also induced significantly elevated ClfB-specific serum IgG titres in mice compared to the control group.
selection_reasoning: This is a key method and principal finding supporting the vaccine potential of ClfB.

fact: Antibodies induced by ClfB vaccination inhibit the binding of ClfB-expressing bacteria to loricrin.
source_span: We confirmed that these antibodies were functional by investigating their ability to inhibit L. lactis expressing ClfB to bind to immobilised loricrin.
selection_reasoning: This functional evidence supports the mechanism of vaccine-induced protection.

fact: ClfB is a surface protein of Staphylococcus aureus that facilitates nasal colonization by binding to host ligands loricrin and cytokeratin 10.
source_span: Previous to this study , the main function attributed to ClfB was in facilitating S . aureus nasal colonization due to its ability to bind host ligands loricrin and cytokeratin 10 in the anterior nares [13–15].
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the known role of ClfB and sets the stage for investigating its role in skin infections.

fact: This study identifies ClfB as a virulence factor that contributes to the pathogenesis of Staphylococcus aureus skin and soft tissue infections (SSTIs).

fact: Using a ClfB mutant strain of the clinically relevant CA-MRSA USA300, the study demonstrates that ClfB is important for early abscess formation during skin infection.

selection_reasoning: This mechanistic insight supports the role of ClfB in SSTI pathogenesis and vaccine targeting.

fact: Loricrin, a host ligand for ClfB, is present not only in the outer skin layers but also within the abscess wall during infection, suggesting it facilitates bacterial binding and abscess development.

selection_reasoning: This fact links host-pathogen interaction to disease pathology, important for understanding infection mechanisms.

fact: Loricrin-deficient mice infected with S. aureus develop smaller abscesses with lower bacterial burden and reduced pathology compared to wild-type mice, indicating the importance of the ClfB-loricrin interaction in SSTIs.
source_span: Lor-/- mice infected s . c . with LAC::lux formed significantly smaller abscess , with lower bacterial burden and reduced pathology compared to WT infected mice , suggesting that the interaction between S . aureus and loricrin is crucial during SSTIs.
selection_reasoning: This genetic evidence supports the critical role of the ClfB-loricrin interaction in infection severity.

selection_reasoning: This finding suggests a potential therapeutic approach targeting the ClfB-loricrin interaction.

fact: Vaccination with ClfB combined with the CpG adjuvant induces antigen-specific cellular immune responses, including CD4+ and CD8+ T cells producing IFNγ, IL-17, and IL-22 in mice.

selection_reasoning: This describes the key immune responses elicited by the vaccine candidate, relevant to vaccine efficacy.

fact: Vaccination with ClfB combined with CpG also induces significant levels of ClfB-specific neutralizing antibodies in mice.

selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the vaccine's ability to stimulate both humoral and cellular immunity.

fact: Mice vaccinated with ClfB plus CpG adjuvant develop significantly smaller abscess lesions and have reduced bacterial burden during Staphylococcus aureus skin infection compared to control mice.

fact: Vaccination with CpG adjuvant alone does not provide protection against Staphylococcus aureus skin infection compared to PBS control.

selection_reasoning: This fact clarifies that protection is due to the ClfB antigen, not the adjuvant alone.

fact: IL-17 and IL-22 cytokine responses are important for protection during cutaneous Staphylococcus aureus infection by promoting neutrophil recruitment and antimicrobial peptide production.

fact: The CpG adjuvant used in this study is considered a promising adjuvant for future infectious disease vaccines due to its low reactogenicity and strong immune-stimulating properties.

fact: ClfB promotes neutrophil recruitment to the infection site and drives local production of antimicrobial peptides, which are important for effective clearance of Staphylococcus aureus.

selection_reasoning: This summarizes the key biochemical pathways involved in DHF pathogenesis.

fact: In the recovery phase of DHF, bile acid biosynthesis and phospholipid catabolism pathways remain altered, while other metabolic pathways return to normal.
source_span: In the recovery phase , the bile acid biosynthesis and phospholipid catabolism pathways were still altered , while other metabolic pathways were no longer disturbed in DHF patients .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights persistent metabolic disturbances after acute dengue infection.

fact: Increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) and reactive nitrogen species (NOS) have been reported in dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF) patients.
source_span: Indeed , increased ROS and NOS have been reported in DHF patients [37] .
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the oxidative stress context relevant to DHF pathogenesis.

fact: Phenylalanine levels are higher in dengue fever (DF) patients than in healthy controls, and even further increased in DHF patients compared to DF patients.
source_span: Furthermore , we have previously found higher levels of phenylalaninein DF patients than in healthy controls . In this study , when compared to DF patients , a further increase of phenylalanine in DHF patients was observed .
selection_reasoning: This finding links phenylalanine accumulation to disease severity and is a key metabolic marker.

fact: The accumulation of phenylalanine in dengue patients is proposed to result from elevated oxidative stress that oxidizes tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4), depleting its pool.
source_span: We have proposed that the accumulation of phenylalanine was due to elevated oxidative stress status in dengue patients where superoxide and peroxynitrite increase oxidation of tetrahydrobiopterin ( BH4 ) , thereby depleting the available BH4 pool [38] .
selection_reasoning: This mechanistic insight connects oxidative stress to metabolic disruption in DHF.

fact: BH4 is a co-factor for phenylalanine hydroxylase, the enzyme that converts phenylalanine to tyrosine.
source_span: BH4 is a co-factor for phenylalanine ( 4 ) -hydroxylase ( PHA ) , an enzyme required for converting phenylalanine to tyrosine .
selection_reasoning: This biochemical fact is necessary to understand the metabolic pathway affected in DHF.

fact: Higher phenylalanine levels indicate increased oxidative stress in DHF patients.
source_span: Thus , higher level of phenylalanine also indicates increased oxidative stress in DHF patients .
selection_reasoning: This summarizes the significance of phenylalanine as a biomarker of oxidative stress in DHF.

fact: Decreased uric acid levels in DHF patients may impair the ability to scavenge reactive oxygen and nitrogen species.
source_span: Together , decreased uric acid could result in impaired ability to scavenge the ROS and NOS in DHF patients .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights a potential mechanism contributing to oxidative damage in DHF.

fact: Systemic uric acid administration can increase serum antioxidant capacity in healthy volunteers, suggesting a potential intervention strategy for DHF.
source_span: It had been shown that systemic uric acid administration could increase serum antioxidant capacity in healthy volunteers [39] , which might be a potential intervention strategy of the condition of DHF .
selection_reasoning: This translational implication suggests a possible therapeutic approach for DHF.

fact: Anti-inflammatory responses help modulate pro-inflammatory processes to prevent excessive inflammation in dengue fever (DF) patients.
source_span: In our previous studies , we have shown that anti-inflammatory responses played an important role in modulating pro-inflammatory processes to prevent the development of pathologies by excessive or prolonged inflammation in DF patients ,
selection_reasoning: This background explains immune regulation relevant to disease progression.

Interestingly , when compared to DF patients , decreased levels of acylcarnitine were found in DHF patients in this study , indicating DHF actually induced less disturbance in fatty acid β-oxidation than DF .

fact: Metabolomics approaches can identify metabolites associated with distinct disease outcomes of dengue infection.
source_span: Nevertheless , both studies showed that metabolomics approach could identify metabolites associated with distinct disease outcomes of dengue infection .
selection_reasoning: This supports the study’s methodological relevance and significance.

fact: This study identified differentially expressed metabolites and metabolic pathways linked to DHF in both the critical and recovery phases of dengue infection.
