selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding summarizing the study’s main contribution.

fact: Altered metabolic pathways identified in DHF might serve as therapeutic targets to alleviate the disease.
source_span: These results provide insights into the mechanisms of DHF pathogenesis , and certain altered pathways might serve as therapeutic targets to alleviate DHF .
selection_reasoning: This highlights the clinical and translational significance of the findings.

fact: Abundance of substrate receptor subunits of Cullin-RING ubiquitin ligases (CRLs) is tightly controlled to maintain the full repertoire of CRLs and prevent sequestration of core components.
source_span: Abundance of substrate receptor subunits of Cullin-RING ubiquitin ligases ( CRLs ) is tightly controlled to maintain the full repertoire of CRLs . Unbalanced levels can lead to sequestration of CRL core components by a few overabundant substrate receptors .
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the biological importance of regulating CRL substrate receptor levels, setting the stage for the study.

fact: Misregulation of substrate receptor components of CRLs, especially SCF ligases, has been associated with numerous diseases including cancer.
source_span: Numerous diseases , including cancer , have been associated with misregulation of substrate receptor components , particularly for the largest class of CRLs , the SCF ligases .
selection_reasoning: This fact motivates the study by linking CRL substrate receptor regulation to disease relevance.

fact: F-box proteins, the substrate receptors of SCF ligases, are regulated by autocatalytic ubiquitylation within the intact SCF complex followed by proteasome-mediated degradation.
source_span: One relevant mechanism that controls abundance of their substrate receptors , the F-box proteins , is autocatalytic ubiquitylation by intact SCF complex followed by proteasome-mediated degradation .
selection_reasoning: This describes the known mechanism controlling F-box protein levels, providing context for the new findings.

fact: The yeast F-box protein Met30 is regulated by an additional degradation pathway that targets Met30 dissociated from Skp1 and requires the cullin component Cdc53/Cul1 but is independent of Skp1.
source_span: Here we describe an additional pathway for regulation of F-box proteins on the example of yeast Met30 . This ubiquitylation and degradation pathway acts on Met30 that is dissociated from Skp1 . Unexpectedly , this pathway required the cullin component Cdc53/Cul1 but was independent of the other central SCF component Skp1 .
selection_reasoning: This is a principal novel finding of the study, identifying a non-canonical degradation pathway for Met30.

fact: The non-canonical degradation pathway of Met30 that is independent of Skp1 is critical for chromosome stability and defense against heavy metal stress in yeast.
source_span: We demonstrated that this non-canonical degradation pathway is critical for chromosome stability and effective defense against heavy metal stress .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the biological significance and functional importance of the newly discovered pathway.

fact: SCFMet30 coordinates metabolic pathways of sulfur-containing compounds with cell cycle progression and regulates the transcription factor Met4.
source_span: In Saccharomyces cerevisiae , Met30 is one of three essential F-box proteins . SCFMet30 coordinates metabolic pathways of sulfur containing compounds with cell cycle progression . The transcription factor Met4 is a key target of SCFMet30 .
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the biological role of Met30 and why its regulation matters.

fact: Cadmium exposure induces dissociation of Met30 from Skp1, inhibiting SCFMet30 activity and triggering glutathione production and cell cycle arrest to protect cells.
source_span: Cadmium exposure induces active dissociation of Met30 from Skp1 , thereby inhibiting SCFMet30 and inducing glutathione production and cell cycle arrest , which together protect cellular integrity .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides context for the physiological condition under which unbound Met30 accumulates and needs to be regulated.

fact: During cadmium stress, Met30 transcription is strongly induced, increasing the pool of unbound Met30 that is not associated with core SCF components.
source_span: In addition , Met30 transcription is induced by over seven fold during cadmium stress , which further increases the amount of Met30 that is not associated with core SCF components ( referred to as unbound or ‘Skp1-free’ Met30 ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains why unbound Met30 accumulates during stress, necessitating additional degradation mechanisms.

fact: The well-known autocatalytic degradation pathway cannot act on Met30 when it is dissociated from Skp1, but Met30 degradation is maintained and even slightly increased during cadmium stress.
source_span: We were interested in how cells cope with the generated excess of Met30 because the well-described autocatalytic F-box protein degradation pathway [10 , 11] cannot act on Met30 during these conditions . Interestingly , degradation of the F-box protein Met30 was maintained and even slightly induced in response to cadmium stress ( Fig 1A ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact motivates the discovery of the new degradation pathway by showing the limitation of the known mechanism.

fact: A mutant form of Met30 lacking its F-box domain, which cannot bind Skp1, is constitutively unstable even without cadmium stress, indicating the presence of a constitutive degradation pathway for unbound Met30.
source_span: A mutant form of Met30 lacking its entire F-box domain ( Met30ΔFbox ) was constitutively unstable even though cells did not experience cadmium stress ( Fig 1B ) . Rapid degradation of Met30ΔFbox was observed both in cycloheximide chase and promoter shut-off experiments , indicating that components of this degradation pathway are constitutively present and that new protein synthesis is not required ( S1A
selection_reasoning: This experimental finding supports the existence of a Skp1-independent degradation pathway acting on unbound Met30.

fact: The SCF core components Cdc53, Rbx1, and the ubiquitin conjugating enzyme Cdc34 are involved in the Skp1-independent ubiquitylation and degradation of unbound Met30.
source_span: This degradation pathway targets Met30 that is detached from Skp1 and involves the SCF core components Cdc53 and Rbx1 , as well as the cognate SCF ubiquitin conjugating enzyme Cdc34 . Importantly , this ubiquitylation pathway does not require Skp1 ( Skp1-independent Cul1-dependent ubiquitylation ) and suggests a function of Cdc53/Cul1 that is independent from association with Skp1 .
selection_reasoning: This fact details the molecular components of the newly identified degradation pathway, central to the study's main claim.

fact: Disruption of the Met30-Skp1 interaction induces rapid degradation of the F-box protein Met30.
source_span: Collectively these results demonstrate that disruption of the Met30-Skp1 interaction , by either active signal-induced dissociation ( cadmium stress ) or by mutations in Met30 or Skp1 , induces rapid degradation of the F-box protein Met30 .
selection_reasoning: This is a core finding linking Met30-Skp1 interaction disruption to Met30 degradation, central to the study's main question.

fact: Met30 that cannot bind Skp1 due to mutations in its F-box domain is constitutively unstable even without cadmium stress.
source_span: A mutant form of Met30 lacking its entire F-box domain ( Met30ΔFbox ) was constitutively unstable even though cells did not experience cadmium stress ( Fig 1B ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact establishes the role of the F-box domain in Met30 stability, important background for understanding the degradation mechanism.

fact: The ubiquitin-proteasome system is involved in degradation of Met30 that is free from Skp1.
source_span: Inhibition of proteasome activity with MG-132 led to stabilization of Met30ΔFbox , suggesting that the ubiquitin proteasome pathway is involved in degradation of ‘Skp1-free’ Met30 ( Fig 2A ) .
selection_reasoning: Identifying the degradation pathway is a key mechanistic insight relevant to the study's principal findings.

fact: Degradation of Skp1-free Met30 depends on the canonical SCF E2 enzyme Cdc34.
source_span: Surprisingly , degradation of Met30ΔFbox was dependent on the canonical SCF E2 , Cdc34 ( Fig 2B ) .
selection_reasoning: This finding reveals an unexpected requirement for a known ubiquitin conjugating enzyme, highlighting a novel aspect of the degradation mechanism.

fact: The cullin-1 protein Cdc53 is essential for degradation of Skp1-free Met30, even though Skp1 is not involved.
source_span: Unexpectedly , Cdc53 was indispensable for Met30ΔFbox degradation , because inactivation of the temperature sensitive cdc53-1 allele blocked degradation ( Fig 2B ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact identifies a key component of the degradation pathway, indicating a novel Skp1-independent function of Cdc53.

fact: The RING finger protein Rbx1 is required for efficient degradation of Skp1-free Met30.
source_span: Consistent with these results Met30ΔFbox degradation was greatly reduced in a strain expressing a 13Myc-tagged version of the RING finger component Rbx1 , which has previously been shown to be a hypomorph allele that results in reduced SCF function at high temperature [32] ( Fig 2B ) .
selection_reasoning: This supports the involvement of SCF core components in the degradation pathway, important for understanding the mechanism.

fact: Met30 degradation when unbound to Skp1 is independent of the transcription factor Met4.
source_span: Analysis of Met30ΔFbox degradation in met4Δ mutants showed that it was not involved in degradation of ‘Skp1-free’ Met30 ( S2A Fig ) .
selection_reasoning: This clarifies that Met4 does not mediate this degradation, refining the understanding of pathway specificity.

fact: Degradation of Skp1-free Met30 is independent of the cullin regulator Lag2 (Cand1 homolog).
source_span: Deletion of LAG2 failed to stabilize Met30ΔFbox demonstrating that degradation of ‘Skp1-free’ Met30 is independent of Lag2 ( S2B Fig ) .
selection_reasoning: This excludes a known cullin regulator from involvement, narrowing down the mechanism.

fact: Skp1 protein depletion using a temperature inducible degron system does not affect degradation of Skp1-free Met30.
source_span: Consistent with results using temperature sensitive alleles of skp1 , Met30ΔFbox degradation was unaffected when Skp1 function was blocked using the skp1-td strategy ( Fig 3C ) .
selection_reasoning: This confirms the Skp1-independence of the degradation pathway using an independent method.

fact: The study reveals a novel proteolytic pathway that targets unbound Met30 to prevent accumulation of excess unbound F-box protein.
source_span: These results suggest a proteolytic pathway that recognizes unbound ‘Skp1-free’ Met30 to avoid accumulation of excess unbound Met30 , which could bind substrates and shield them from recognition by fully assembled SCFMet30 complexes .
selection_reasoning: This is a principal conclusion highlighting the biological significance of the findings.

fact: Attenuation of Skp1 in yeast cells causes cell cycle arrest with elongated multibudded cell morphology, indicating inactivation of SCFCdc4 and SCFMet30 functions.
source_span: Attenuation of Skp1 induced the expected biological response such as cell cycle arrest with elongated multibudded cell morphology indicative of SCFCdc4 inactivation , and block of SCFMet30 function as assayed by loss of ubiquitylated forms of Met4
selection_reasoning: This fact provides important background on the biological role of Skp1 and its impact on SCF complexes, which is central to the study's focus.

fact: Met30ΔFbox degradation occurs independently of Skp1 function in yeast cells.
source_span: Met30ΔFbox degradation was unaffected when Skp1 function was blocked using the skp1-td strategy
selection_reasoning: This finding challenges the canonical view of SCF complex function and is a core discovery of the study.

fact: The degradation of Met30 in the absence of Skp1 depends on the cullin protein Cdc53.
source_span: The experiments with skp1 single and skp1 cdc53 double mutants strongly suggested that the ‘Skp1-free’ degradation pathway for Met30 was dependent on Cdc53 and independent of Skp1
selection_reasoning: Identifying Cdc53 as essential for Skp1-independent degradation is a key mechanistic insight.

fact: A Cdc53 mutant (Cdc53Y133R) that cannot interact with Skp1 still supports degradation of Met30ΔFbox.
source_span: Immunopurification experiments confirmed that Cdc53Y133R does not interact with Skp1 in vivo ... Importantly ... Cdc53Y133R supported degradation of Met30ΔFbox to the same extent as wild type Cdc53
selection_reasoning: This result directly supports the hypothesis that Cdc53 can mediate degradation independently of Skp1.

fact: A specific region of Met30 adjacent to the F-box domain (amino acids 137–187) contains a degron required for Skp1-independent degradation.
source_span: Deletion of the N terminal amino acids adjacent to the F-box motif ( amino acids 137–187 ) was sufficient for Met30ΔFbox stabilization
selection_reasoning: Identifying the degron region is critical for understanding how Skp1-independent degradation is targeted.

fact: Mutation of two hydrophobic residues (M178E and I179E) within the degron region blocks Skp1-independent degradation of Met30.
source_span: Mutation of both residues to glutamate ( M178E and I179E ) blocked ‘Skp1-free’ Met30ΔFbox degradation
selection_reasoning: Pinpointing key residues essential for degradation clarifies the molecular mechanism.

fact: Under normal growth conditions, the majority of Met30 is targeted for proteolysis via the Skp1-independent degradation pathway.
source_span: Introduction of the same mutations into full length Met30 dramatically stabilized Met30
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the physiological relevance of the Skp1-independent degradation pathway.

fact: Mass spectrometry failed to identify any adaptor proteins other than Skp1 that mediate Cdc53-dependent degradation of Met30ΔFbox.
source_span: We failed to identify any proteins that fit these criteria ... suggested that perhaps Cdc53/Rbx1 might directly bind Met30 without an adaptor protein
selection_reasoning: This negative result supports the novel idea that Cdc53 can directly bind substrates without an adaptor.

fact: Cdc53 can bind directly to the N-terminal region of Met30 in vitro in the absence of Skp1, and this binding is reduced by the M178E/I179E mutations.
source_span: In the absence of Skp1 , Cdc53 bound effectively to ( MBP ) -Met30 ( 1–186 ) and binding was significantly reduced when ( MBP ) -Met30 ( 1–186 ) M178E/I179E was used as the bait
selection_reasoning: This biochemical evidence confirms direct interaction between Cdc53 and Met30 independent of Skp1.

fact: Purified Cdc53/Rbx1 complex expressed in bacteria can directly bind to the N-terminal region of Met30 without any other yeast proteins, and this binding is reduced by the degron mutations.
source_span: Cdc53/Rbx1 could specifically interact with ( MBP ) -Met30 ( 1–186 ) and binding was significantly decreased in the degron mutations that stabilized Met30 in vivo
selection_reasoning: This finding demonstrates that Cdc53/Rbx1 alone is sufficient for substrate recognition, supporting a novel degradation mechanism.

fact: The site on Cdc53 that binds Met30 in the Skp1-independent pathway is distinct from the Skp1-binding domain.
source_span: Cdc53 expressed in E . coli is spontaneously cleaved at the N-terminal region ... the removed residues 1–266 harbor the Skp1-binding region . Therefore , Met30 can interact with Cdc53/Rbx1 in vitro at a site distinct from the Skp1 binding domain
selection_reasoning: This fact clarifies the molecular basis for Skp1-independent substrate recognition by Cdc53.

fact: Met30 can directly interact with the Cdc53/Rbx1 complex in vitro at a site distinct from the Skp1 binding domain of Cdc53.
source_span: Therefore , Met30 can interact with Cdc53/Rbx1 in vitro at a site distinct from the Skp1 binding domain of Cdc53 .
selection_reasoning: This establishes a key molecular interaction central to the study's investigation of Skp1-independent degradation.

fact: The Cdc53/Rbx1 complex can ubiquitylate 'Skp1-free' Met30 in vitro, but the ubiquitylation reaction is inefficient and slow.
source_span: ( MBP ) -Met30 ( 1–186 ) was ubiquitylated in vitro and the reaction was dependent on Cdc53/Rbx1 complex ( S4A Fig ) . However , the reaction is very inefficient and only a small fraction of Met30 ( 1–186 ) was ubiquitylated even after 16 h incubation of the reaction .
selection_reasoning: This finding supports the existence of a Skp1-independent ubiquitylation mechanism for Met30, a core study claim.

fact: Mutations in Met30 that stabilize it in vivo reduce its ubiquitylation by Cdc53/Rbx1 in vitro.
source_span: To test whether this weak activity was specific for the ‘Skp1-free’ degradation pathway of Met30 , we compared ubiquitylation in ( MBP ) -Met30 ( 1–186 ) and ( MBP ) -Met30 ( 1–186 ) M178E/I179E mutant . Ubiquitylation of ( MBP ) -Met30 ( 1–186 ) M178E/I179E was visibly reduced ( S4B Fig ) .
selection_reasoning: This links specific degron mutations to reduced ubiquitylation, supporting the mechanism of Skp1-independent degradation.

fact: The observed weak ubiquitylation activity of Cdc53/Rbx1 on Met30 suggests involvement of additional factors or post-translational modifications for efficient ubiquitylation.
source_span: This suggests possible involvement of another factor or a post-translational modification , which is likely not required for binding Cdc53/Rbx1 to Met30 but is required for effective ubiquitylation of the substrate .
selection_reasoning: This highlights a limitation and points to complexity in the Skp1-independent degradation pathway.

fact: There is evidence for a Skp1-independent degradation pathway for several F-box proteins, including Met30, Cdc4, and Ctf13.
source_span: Thus , these results provide evidence for existence of an additional , Skp1-independent , degradation pathway for several F-box proteins , which appears to target F-box proteins that are not bound to the SCF core complex .
selection_reasoning: This generalizes the study’s findings beyond Met30, indicating broader biological significance.

fact: Degradation of the F-box protein Cdc4 continues even when Skp1 is depleted, indicating a Skp1-independent degradation mechanism.
source_span: In skp1-td mutants , Cdc4 was slightly more stable compared to wild type cells , but still degraded rapidly even though Skp1 was depleted as evident by deubiquitylated Met4 ( Fig 7B ) and elongated , multibudded cells .
selection_reasoning: This supports the existence of a Skp1-independent degradation pathway for F-box proteins.

fact: The Skp1-independent degradation pathway limits the abundance of 'free' F-box proteins and may prevent substrate shielding by excess unbound F-box proteins.
source_span: Such a mechanism for F-box protein homeostasis could be important not only to limit the overall abundance , but also to limit competition for substrates between assembled SCF ligases and the ‘free’ F-box protein subunits , which could lead to substrate shielding and thus prevent substrate ubiquitylation .
selection_reasoning: This explains the biological significance and functional role of the Skp1-independent degradation pathway.

fact: Yeast cells expressing a Met30 mutant (M178E/I179E) that blocks Skp1-independent degradation show increased Met30 protein abundance.
source_span: As expected , Met30 displayed increased abundance in cells expressing the degron point mutant in comparison to those expressing the wild type allele ( Fig 8A ) .
selection_reasoning: This demonstrates the functional impact of blocking the Skp1-independent degradation pathway in vivo.

fact: Despite increased Met30 abundance in the Met30M178E/I179E mutant, ubiquitylation of the SCFMet30 substrate Met4 is slightly reduced.
source_span: Interestingly , despite the increased protein abundance of Met30M178E/I179E steady-state ubiquitylation of the major SCFMet30 substrate , the transcription factor Met4 , [25] , was slightly reduced ( Fig 8A ) .
selection_reasoning: This suggests that excess unbound Met30 may interfere with normal substrate ubiquitylation.

fact: The Skp1-independent degradation pathway is important for recovery from cadmium-induced stress in yeast.
source_span: We reasoned that the Skp1-independent degradation pathway should be particularly important for the recovery from heavy metal stress . Cadmium exposure leads to dissociation of Met30 from Skp1 [24 , 26 , 27] thereby generating a burst of ‘Skp1-free’ Met30 , which needs to be controlled by the ‘Skp1-free’ F-box protein degradation pathway .
selection_reasoning: This links the pathway to a physiologically relevant stress response.

fact: Yeast cells expressing the Met30M178E/I179E mutant are more sensitive to cadmium stress and exhibit growth arrest.
source_span: Cells expressing Met30M178E/I179E were significantly more sensitive and exhibited a growth arrest in response to cadmium stress ( Fig 8B ) .
selection_reasoning: This shows the functional consequence of impaired Skp1-independent degradation under stress.

fact: Excess dissociated Met30 in the Met30M178E/I179E mutant may bind Met4 and shield it from ubiquitylation, maintaining cell cycle arrest during cadmium stress recovery.
source_span: We hypothesized that excess dissociated Met30 may bind Met4 and shield it from ubiquitylation by fully assembled SCFMet30 ligase during the recovery phase . The cell cycle checkpoint arrest , initially induced by deubiquitylated Met4 to cope with cadmium stress , may therefore be erroneously maintained in MET30M178E/I179E mutants resulting in apparent cadmium sensitivity .
selection_reasoning: This provides a mechanistic explanation for the observed cadmium sensitivity phenotype.

fact: Excess dissociated Met30 can bind Met4 and prevent its ubiquitylation by the SCFMet30 ligase during recovery from cadmium stress.
source_span: We hypothesized that excess dissociated Met30 may bind Met4 and shield it from ubiquitylation by fully assembled SCFMet30 ligase during the recovery phase.
selection_reasoning: This explains a key molecular mechanism underlying cadmium sensitivity and cell cycle arrest recovery, central to the study's findings.

fact: The cell cycle checkpoint arrest induced by deubiquitylated Met4 to cope with cadmium stress is maintained longer in MET30M178E/I179E mutants, causing apparent cadmium sensitivity.
source_span: The cell cycle checkpoint arrest, initially induced by deubiquitylated Met4 to cope with cadmium stress, may therefore be erroneously maintained in MET30M178E/I179E mutants resulting in apparent cadmium sensitivity.
selection_reasoning: This links the mutant phenotype to a failure in cell cycle recovery, a principal finding relevant to the study's biological significance.

fact: Deletion of MET32 suppresses the growth defect of MET30M178E/I179E mutants under cadmium stress by preventing prolonged Met4-induced cell cycle arrest.
source_span: We tested this hypothesis by deleting MET32 in MET30M178E/I179E mutants... deletion of MET32 suppressed the growth defect of cells expressing Met30M178E/I179E under cadmium stress.
selection_reasoning: This genetic evidence supports the mechanism of Met4-mediated cell cycle arrest causing cadmium sensitivity, a key experimental result.

fact: Met4 target genes MET3 and GSH1 are derepressed in Met30M178E/I179E mutants, confirming untimely Met4 activation.
source_span: Consistent with this idea, two tested Met4 target genes, MET3 and GSH1, were derepressed in Met30M178E/I179E mutants confirming untimely Met4 activation.
selection_reasoning: This molecular evidence confirms the functional consequence of excess dissociated Met30 on Met4 activity, central to the study's conclusions.

fact: The ‘Skp1-free’ F-box protein degradation pathway prevents substrate shielding effects by degrading excess unbound F-box proteins like Met30.
source_span: Together, these results indicate that the ‘Skp1-free’ F-box protein degradation pathway plays an important role in cellular function to prevent substrate shielding effects by excess unbound F-box proteins.
selection_reasoning: This identifies the novel degradation pathway as a key regulatory mechanism, a principal conceptual advance of the study.

fact: Met30M178E/I179E mutants show increased chromosome loss, suggesting additional cellular defects linked to stabilized Met30.
source_span: In addition to enhanced cadmium sensitivity, Met30M178E/I179E mutants displayed increased chromosome loss.
selection_reasoning: This finding extends the significance of the mutant phenotype beyond cadmium sensitivity, indicating broader cellular impact.

fact: The study describes a novel degradation pathway targeting F-box proteins that are dissociated from Skp1, distinct from autoubiquitylation.
source_span: We describe a novel pathway for regulation of F-box protein abundance in addition to autoubiquitylation that specifically targets F-box proteins that are dissociated from Skp1.
selection_reasoning: This is a core methodological and conceptual claim about the mechanism regulating F-box protein levels.

fact: The ‘Skp1-free’ F-box protein degradation pathway maintains F-box protein homeostasis by degrading unbound F-box proteins via the Cdc53/Rbx1 ligase.
source_span: F-box proteins that associate with Skp1 form functional ligases while those that do not, are recognized by the ‘Skp1-free’ F-box protein degradation pathway and degraded by the Cdc53/Rbx1 ligase thereby preventing competition between F-box proteins.
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the biological significance and mechanism of the newly described degradation pathway.

fact: Degradation of unbound F-box proteins may serve as a quality control mechanism to remove damaged F-box proteins that could otherwise shield substrates from degradation.
source_span: Degradation of F-box proteins that are not bound to Skp1 may also provide an important quality control mechanism to remove damaged F-box proteins.
selection_reasoning: This implication highlights the physiological importance of the pathway beyond abundance regulation.

fact: The ‘Skp1-free’ F-box protein degradation pathway is particularly important for Met30 because Met4 ubiquitylation does not induce Met4 degradation, causing Met4 to remain bound to Met30 and prevent autoubiquitylation-based degradation.
source_span: The ‘Skp1-free’ F-box protein degradation pathway is of particular importance for Met30. First, because Met4 ubiquitylation does not induce its degradation under normal growth conditions, Met4 remains associated with Met30 and therefore prevents the canonical F-box-protein degradation pathway through autoubiquitylation.
selection_reasoning: This explains why Met30 relies on the novel pathway, a key mechanistic insight.

fact: Heavy metal stress induces dissociation of Met30 from Skp1, increasing ‘Skp1-free’ Met30 that interferes with recovery from cadmium stress when the degradation pathway is blocked.
source_span: Second, heavy metal stress induces active dissociation of Met30 from Skp1 resulting in a burst of ‘Skp1-free’ Met30, which interferes with recovery from cadmium stress when the ‘Skp1-free’ degradation pathway is blocked.
selection_reasoning: This links environmental stress to pathway activation and physiological consequences, central to the study's significance.

fact: Other essential yeast F-box proteins, Cdc4 and Ctf13, are also degraded in the absence of Skp1, suggesting the pathway is a common mechanism to restrict F-box protein abundance outside the SCF complex.
source_span: Apart from Met30, the two other essential yeast F-box proteins—Cdc4 and Ctf13 are also degraded in the absence of Skp1, suggesting that this pathway is a common mechanism to restrict F-box protein abundance outside the SCF complex.
selection_reasoning: This generalizes the pathway beyond Met30, increasing its biological relevance.

fact: Not all F-box proteins are subject to the ‘Skp1-free’ degradation pathway; for example, Grr1 is stabilized when its F-box region is deleted or Skp1 is inactivated.
